note: Hand-curated finding aids for archival collections that have no NARA catalog record. All 438 presidential-library clusters in collection-authority.json carry a null naId, and that is structural: the libraries sit outside every NARA record group, so the record-group-filtered catalogue harvest cannot reach them. What the repositories publish instead is a finding aid, which is what a researcher needs. Seeded (#355 / N-4) with the two rows measurement showed are containers rather than collections: Carter's National Security Affairs (3,591 documents splitting 57.5% Brzezinski Material / 40.2% Staff Material) and the Library of Congress Manuscript Division (958 documents naming 12 distinct personal-papers collections). Every URL was fetched before it was written here. Extended with Reagan's Executive Secretariat NSC series (10 targets, 501 of 572 documents) and Nixon's White House Special Files (4 targets, 90 of 156). Nixon's 'Staff Member and Office Files' is deliberately absent: it is a LEVEL containing per-person aids, not a unit with an aid of its own, so no single URL is honest for it.

resolution.title: National Security Advisor (Brzezinski and Staff Material)
resolution.rationale: The whole Records of the Office of the National Security Advisor, 775 linear feet — what an unqualified 'National Security Affairs' citation names. The library's own finding aid states the records 'were kept in two large sub-collections given the titles "Brzezinski Material" and "Staff Material"', which is why the two branches below share this aid.

resolution.title: National Security Advisor (Brzezinski and Staff Material)
resolution.rationale: Series NSA 1–16 of the collection. NARA assigns identifiers to the parent collection (560131) and to each of the 32 series, but to no intermediate sub-collection, so this level carries no NAID of its own. The aliases are spellings the corpus actually prints.

resolution.title: National Security Advisor (Brzezinski and Staff Material)
resolution.rationale: Series NSA 17–32 of the same collection. The library publishes no separate Staff Material aid, so this collection-level aid — whose own title names both branches — is the most precise honest target.

resolution.title: Zbigniew Brzezinski Material — Office Files (NSA 15)
resolution.rationale: Series NSA 15, containers 1–127. Identified by its sub-series rather than by name: the scope note reads 'divided into a Country Chron File and a Subject Chron File', and the corpus cites exactly those two. NSA 17 is also titled 'Office Files' but contains neither, so the 'Brzezinski' qualifier is decisive. The linked page is the collection aid; NARA publishes the series identifier in the PDF.

resolution.title: Staff Material — North/South Files (NSA 24)
resolution.rationale: Series NSA 24, an exact match to the citation segment. The library publishes no per-series page, so the link is the collection aid.

resolution.title: Zbigniew Brzezinski Papers
resolution.rationale: A DIFFERENT collection from the NSA Brzezinski Material despite the similar name: accession 92-03 under Brzezinski's own 1992 instrument of gift, against the NSA collection's accession 80-1 under Carter's 1981 gift. The NSA finding aid lists it separately as related material held in the same repository.

resolution.title: Henry A. Kissinger Papers, Part I
resolution.rationale: Part I covers Kissinger's service as National Security Adviser 1969–1975 and Secretary of State 1973–1977, in 26 series spanning 1957–1982 — the FRUS era. Part II is at Yale and is distinguishable by its citations; the corpus contains none. Library of Congress collections carry no NARA identifier.

resolution.title: W. Averell Harriman Papers
resolution.rationale: W. Averell Harriman (1891–1986), 346,760 items. Not Pamela Harriman (1920–1997) or Florence Jaffray Harriman (1870–1967), both of whom the Library also holds.

resolution.title: Alexander Meigs Haig Papers
resolution.rationale: Alexander Meigs Haig, Jr. (1924–2010), 161,000 items. Not the Douglas Haig, Earl (1861–1928) papers the Library also holds.

resolution.title: James R. Schlesinger Papers
resolution.rationale: James R. Schlesinger, Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Energy — not Arthur M. Schlesinger, Jr., whose papers FRUS cites at the Kennedy Library under a separate row.

resolution.title: Caspar W. Weinberger Papers
resolution.rationale: Caspar W. Weinberger, Secretary of Defense 1981–1987.

resolution.title: Elliot L. Richardson Papers
resolution.rationale: Elliot L. Richardson, Secretary of Defense, Attorney General and Secretary of Commerce.

resolution.title: Paul H. Nitze Papers
resolution.rationale: Paul H. Nitze, Policy Planning Staff director and arms-control negotiator.

resolution.title: Sol M. Linowitz Papers
resolution.rationale: Sol M. Linowitz, Panama Canal treaty negotiator and Middle East envoy.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Country File: Records, 1981-1985
resolution.rationale: A subseries of the NSC Executive Secretariat's Presidential Acquisitions series, arranged in five geographical regions.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Head of State File: Records, 1981-1989
resolution.rationale: Correspondence between the President and world leaders, arranged by country then chronologically.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Cable File: Records, 1982-1985
resolution.rationale: The aid's span (1982–1985) is narrower than the volumes' coverage; some box inventories show only a range of material.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Subject File: Records, 1981-1985
resolution.rationale: Three series: Memorandum File, Correspondence File, and Cabinet/Cabinet Council Meeting File.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Agency File: Records, 1981-1985
resolution.rationale: Records on specific Executive-branch agencies, including the Secretary of State's evening reports and the Secretary of Defense's weekly briefings.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Trip Files: Records, 1981-1989
resolution.rationale: Two series: Chronological Trip File and Summit File. The aid titles it plural; the citations write it singular.

resolution.rationale: National Security Study Directives — the policy studies commissioned by Senior Interagency Groups, the NSC staff or the National Security Adviser.

resolution.title: President's Office Files (White House Special Files: Staff Member and Office Files)
resolution.rationale: NARA series 876218. Not the Returned Materials Collection, whose own 'White House Special Files' pages describe personal material returned to the Nixon estate — a different body of records from the one these citations name.

resolution.title: President's Personal File (White House Special Files: Staff Member and Office Files)
resolution.rationale: NARA series 595291, whose own title is the plural 'President's Personal Files' the citations use; the library titles the aid singular. 18 sub-series.

resolution.title: Subject Files (White House Special Files)
resolution.rationale: No NARA series record corresponds to this unit — searched at series level several ways — so the absence of an identifier here is a finding, not an omission.

resolution.title: Staff Secretary (White House Special Files: Staff Member and Office Files)
resolution.rationale: NARA series 6004162, titled 'Staff Secretary's Files' as the citations write it; the library titles the aid simply 'Staff Secretary'. Its five series match the aid's.

resolution.title: Executive Secretariat, NSC: Head of State File: Records, 1981-1989
